newsitem.title: USA: Mich approves gas tax hike for roads and bridges.
newsitem.headline: Mich approves gas tax hike for roads and bridges.

text.p: Michigan lawmakers approved a 4-cent-per-gallon gasoline tax increase for road and bridge repairs for fiscal 1998, state budget office spokeswoman Maureen McNulty said Wednesday.
Lawmakers approved the comprehensive roads package early Wednesday providing $300 million for repairs and targeted tax cuts before adjourning until September, McNulty said.

Lawmakers have not completed work on the budget for fiscal 1998 beginning October 1 and will address the transportation budget, capital outlay requests and plans to increase the state building authority's bond cap by $700 million to $2.7 billion when they return, McNulty said.
The bond cap legislation has been under consideration since summer 1996, McNulty noted.
The road funding package also increases trucking fees by $43 million transfers another $43 million from the general fund and increases application of diesel fuel taxes by $28 million.
Included along with the spending for the next fiscal year is a one-time $69 million appropriation of interest from Michigan's budget stabilization fund to fix roads during fiscal 1997.
